title: Yesterday I went
goal: Telling what happened yesterday with verbs that take no object — the easy half of the past tense, fully in place before the hard half arrives in the next unit.
bekal: talk about trips, arrivals, and what happened yesterday
use the past form of objectless verbs, which agrees with the doer
use وم، وې، و، وه as past "was/were"

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — د پرون کیسه
dialogs.intro: Saturday morning. Najib has just come back from Mazar-e Sharif, and Budi wants to hear everything at once.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: How did you go? By car?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نه، په الوتکه کې ولاړم. لار اوږده وه.
lines.baca: nə, pə alwatka ke wlāṛəm. lār ūẓda wa.
lines.id: No, I flew. It was a long trip.
lines.literal: no, in plane in went-I. road long was.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: And what time did you get there?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: ماښام لس بجې راغلم. ډېر ستړی وم.
lines.baca: māṣām las baje rāghləm. ḍer stəṛay wəm.
lines.id: I arrived at ten at night. I was very tired.
lines.literal: evening ten o'clock came-I. very tired was-I.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: هو، هغه هم ولاړه. خو هغه پرون بېرته راغله.
lines.baca: ho, hagha ham wlāṛa. kho hagha parūn berta rāghla.
lines.id: Yes, she went too. But she came back yesterday.
lines.literal: yes, she also went-she. but she yesterday back came-she.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Why did you all go? Was it work?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نه، د ترور واده و. ټوله کورنۍ راټوله شوه.
lines.baca: nə, də tror wāda wə. ṭola kornəy rāṭola shwa.
lines.id: No, my aunt's wedding. The whole family got together.
lines.literal: no, of aunt wedding was. whole family gathered became-she.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: ډېر ښکلی و! درې سوه کسان راغلل.
lines.baca: ḍer ṣkulay wə! dre swa kasān rāghləl.
lines.id: Really beautiful! Three hundred people came.
lines.literal: very beautiful was! three hundred people came-they.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: درې سوه؟ زه هېڅکله دومره لوی واده نه یم لیدلی.
lines.baca: dre swa? zə hetskəla domra loy wāda nə yəm līdəlay.
lines.id: Three hundred? I've never seen a wedding that big.
lines.literal: three hundred? I never that-much big wedding not am seen.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: دلته دا معمولي ده. بل ځل ته هم راځه.
lines.baca: dəlta dā ma'mūlī da. bəl dzal tə ham rādza.
lines.id: That's normal here. Next time you come too.
lines.literal: here this normal is. other time you also come.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: حتماً! خو زه لا نه پوهېږم څنګه ونڅېږم.
lines.baca: hatman! kho zə lā nə poheẓəm tsənga wə́nadzeẓəm.
lines.id: Definitely! But I don't know how to dance yet.
lines.literal: definitely! but I still not understand-I how dance-done-I.

notes: Verbs that take **no object** — go, come, sit, sleep, get up, become — make past sentences that behave sensibly: the doer stays in its usual form, and the verb agrees with the doer. This is the easy half, and this whole unit is spent making it automatic.

⚠️ The verb agrees with the doer's **gender**. Najib says زه **ولاړم**, Zarghuna says زه **ولاړمه**; in the third person, a man is **ولاړ** and a woman **ولاړه**. This is where the gender you set up in unit 2 finally does its full job.

Note that ولاړم is the past of تلل, not of some other verb. Pashto has a few verbs whose past looks nothing like their present — just like *go* and *went* in English, and there's no point fighting it.

Past "was/were" is وم، وې، و، وه، وو. زه ستړی **وم** means "I was tired", واده ښکلی **و** means "the wedding was beautiful". These forms are little more than the letter و and easy for the ear to miss; listen closely.

Afghan weddings really are that big. Three hundred guests is middling, and inviting distant relatives and neighbors is not just politeness. If you're invited, go — turning down a wedding invitation is far more serious than turning down an offer of tea.

The phrase نه یم لیدلی means "I've never seen". This is the perfect form, built from the verb plus a form of "to be". You don't need to make it yourself yet; just recognize the pattern when you hear it.

grammars.title: The past tense of verbs with no object
body: It's built from the verb's past stem plus an ending that agrees with the doer. For the third person singular masculine, the ending is actually **empty** — which is why it often sounds like a word cut short.

Look at the feminine column. ولاړه and راغله are easy to mistake for plurals; only one letter tells them apart. Read both out loud now, because you'll need them every time you tell a story about a woman.

grammars.title: The past of "to be"
body: The past of "to be" is much shorter than the present, and it's built entirely from the letter و. In fast speech it's almost inaudible — listen to the vowel length, not the letter.
Just as in English, the verb is **required**: "yesterday cold" can't stand on its own; the correct form is پرون سوړ **و** ("it was cold yesterday").

blocks.title: Afghan weddings, and their words
items: The word **واده** *wāda* means wedding, **ناوې** *nāwe* the bride, and **زوم** *zūm* the groom.
The music and dance is called **اتڼ** *atáṇ* — the Pashtun circle dance that spins faster and faster, and that you'll be asked to join whether you can dance or not.
The congratulation you'll use: **مبارک شه** *mubārak sha* — "congratulations". The reply is **مننه** or **خدای دې مبارک کړي**.
Invitations are almost always spoken and cover the whole family. If you're invited alone and bring a friend, that's fine — it's the opposite that would be odd.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Why this unit is only half the story
items: Every verb in this unit takes **no object**: go, come, sit, sleep, become. You can't "go something" or "come something".

Once the verb **has an object** — reading a book, eating bread, seeing someone — Pashto rearranges the whole past sentence. The doer moves into the oblique form, and the verb stops agreeing with the doer.
That's what unit 13 is about, and it's the only thing that unit does. Don't skip this unit to get there faster: the past forms on this page are the ground the next unit stands on.
Test yourself before moving on: if you can say "yesterday I went to the market and got there at five" without stopping, you're ready.

exercises.prompt: Change into the past for the doer زه (male).
Fill in the right past form of "to be".

items: Yesterday I went to Mazar-e Sharif.
I came at ten at night.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: پرون زه مزار شریف ته ولاړم. — زه ماښام لس بجې راغلم. — زرغونه هم ولاړه. — زه ډېر ستړی وم. — درې سوه کسان راغلل.
پرون زه مزار ته ولاړم. — زه ډېر ستړی وم. — هغه پرون بېرته راغله. — واده ډېر ښکلی و. — درې سوه کسان راغلل.
wave: Tell your own yesterday in five past sentences, all with objectless verbs: get up, go, arrive, sit, sleep. If you're a woman, make sure every verb ends in ـمه.
